and they became Christians again.
And from him was descended this Nicephorus who became king.
And he was a mighty man, and prudent, and given to fasting and prayer.
And on this account, Elpidius the rebel said to Abd al-Malik, the commander of the army of the Arabs:
"If Nicephorus has become king,
cast away from you this soft garment,
and put on armor and prepare for war."
Now Nicephorus, as soon as he became king,
sent letters to Harun and provoked him.
And they prepared for {OCR? ܓܲܩܪܵܒ݂ܵܐ -> ܠܲܩܪܵܒ݂ܵܐ} war,
and for two months they remained encamped,
and through envoys and letters Nicephorus and Harun were speaking and hearing.
And at last they made peace,
and they sent gifts to one another {OCR? ܓܲܚ̈ܕܵܕܹܐ -> ܠܲܚ̈ܕܵܕܹܐ},
and each one returned to his place.
At this time a certain Qurayshite Muslim,
whose name was Rawhi,
was close in his house to a church.
And at the time of prayer he used to annoy the priest,
and cast at him pellets rolled from dust.
And one of the days, while he was peering in at the time of the sacrifice,
he saw inside the paten which was on the table of life a lamb being cut into pieces.
And when he went down to the priest,
he saw bread that was broken.
And again he went up to the window,
he peered in and saw a lamb.
Then he believed,
and he left his house and went to a monastery and was baptized.
And when news of him reached Harun,
he sent, brought him, and enticed him to return,
but he would not consent.
And when he cast him into irons and imprisoned him for two years, and he did not relent,
he commanded, and his head was cut off with the sword,
and he was hanged on the wall of Raqqa.
And many saw a light that overshadowed him;
and a Christian man from the country of Persia took him down and carried him to his city.
At this time there came to Harun a certain Roman whose name was Thomas, son of Musammar,
and he said
that he was, forsooth, the son of Constantine the king.
And Harun did not {OCR? ܦܸܢ -> ܡܸܢ / ܠܵܐ} neglect him,
but treated him with honor as a king's son.
And in the year 1115 [804 AD],
while Harun was in Persia,
a large army of the Romans went out and plundered {OCR? 1 ܓܐܲܬ݂ܪܵܐ -> ܠܐܲܬ݂ܪܵܐ} the region of Mopsuestia and Anazarba.
And the Arabs overtook them,
and recovered the captives.
And when Harun heard, he came to the city of Callinicus,
and in Nisan he plundered Heraclea.
And Nicephorus went out to make war with him.
He, however, when he saw the great army of the Romans,
sought peace,
and gave up all the prisoners
